problem: The native revision fixtures reached previously untested binary metadata paths. XLS read RRDInfo history fields two bytes early and compared historical sheet maps with the current catalog. Its cell-change reader also treated variable-value size descriptors as physical tail lengths. XLSB expected the wrong user-record order, appended typed records after an existing EOF, used specification subsection numbers as wire IDs for RRd projection, and could not append/remove the latest header while maintaining GUID closure.
changes: Read XLS RRDInfo history flags/interval at offsets 46/48 after the complete four-byte version. Correct synthetic payload builders and test version/history independence.

Validate current BoundSheet8 cardinality against the latest XLS map while retaining historical map framing/uniqueness checks and the authoritative large-workbook omission boundary. Add differing-history and >4112-sheet regressions.

Retain fixed-type old-value wire-size checks and the formula minimum. Treat variable string/formula cbOldVal as its stored size descriptor, not an offset into the compressed/continued tail; add focused compressed-string, short-formula and truncated-fixed-value checks.

Admit native XLSB CUsr-before-BeginUsers order, keep typed user/header additions before explicit EOF, and emit EOF for newly authored typed owners. Preserve the existing bounded unterminated and opaque-trailing-record profiles; refuse typed owners after an explicit end marker.

Use the twelve actual BIFF12 RRd record IDs (405,407,409,412-419,421), leaving subsection numbers and unrelated records opaque. Maintain current/saved header GUID pointers during append/removal while retaining user-reference and final-header deletion refusals.

Add eleven native tests across XLS/XLSX/XLSB plus nine focused regressions. Ten native tests enter the semantic/operation index; the noncanonical XLS User Names check is evidence-only. Correct stale Transaction API names in feature matrices.

specification_evidence.finding: The 50-byte layout places version at 42..46, history flags at 46..48 and interval at 48..50. Native fields are revision 6, version 2 and 30-day history.

Each saved revision set has its own header and tab map, and the native history has varying map sizes. Implementation inference from that per-set scope: enforce current-catalog cardinality on the latest map. Framing and duplicate-identifier checks still apply to every historical map.

Variable old-value descriptors have type-specific size rules, including double-byte string sizing and a formula minimum; they are not physical offsets into a compressed/continued record tail. Fixed-size value rules remain enforced.
Allowed stored versions are 0200/0300/0400/0500/0600. The native legacy export stores 0006; that fixture-profile rejection is retained and separately reviewed.

BrtEOF ends the shared-workbook collection. Native user bytes contain CUsr, BeginUsers, EOF; new typed entries must remain before the existing end marker. Record IDs differ from the numbered 2.4 subsections.

Both the supplied conversion and current public page expose a build-path placeholder for the ABNF. This work combines explicit record definitions and native wire evidence; it does not claim complete ABNF validation.

verification_scope.xls_user_gap: The 536-byte User Names stream has four framing records and no users, but UsrChk is 0006. Its inactive first CbUsr size is 41. The precise InvalidRecord 0198 diagnostic is evidence-only under xls-176, not a passing user-log projection. A conforming native user-log/dependency specimen remains needed.
verification_scope.preservation: All unrelated workbook payloads remain exact. XLSB source relationship XML may be reserialized, with complete attribute equality checked. Newly recreated XLSX owner XML may reorder attributes; comparison preserves namespaces/values/text and record/child order. Source-checked inverses restore prior payloads and graph.
verification_scope.limits: No live users, collaboration, locking, revision application, conflict resolution, formula recalculation or fresh Excel reopen is claimed. Added users/headers are Litchi-authored derivatives. XLS variable bodies remain opaque, and the malformed legacy revision/user profile remains unresolved.
